A loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
The pilot failed to maintain directional control of the airplane while landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree while on short final.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control and the flight instructor's inadequate remedial action during the landing roll, which resulted in a ground loop.

The fracture of the aileron hinge strap due to fatigue crack propagation, which resulted in substantial damage to a wing rib aft of the spar at the outboard aileron cutout. Contributing to the accident was inadequate maintenance inspection.
The pilot's inadequate compensation for the crosswind condition and failure to maintain directional control.

A pre-existing crack in the front spar of the right horizontal stabilizer near a riveted fitting, causing it to fail and separate from the airplane in flight. The biplane pilot’s inadequate visual lookout, which resulted in an on-ground collision with another airplane while taxiing.

The pilot’s inadequate compensation for winds during the landing roll.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during landing.

A partial loss of engine power while on approach to land due to a disconnected throttle control linkage, and the maintenance director's inadequate inspection of the throttle linkage during maintenance.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees and terrain while in cruise flight in marginal visual meteorological conditions.
The pilot’s inadequate preflight inspection and fuel management, which resulted in fuel starvation, a total loss of engine power, and an impact with terrain.
The pilot's selection of unsuitable terrain for takeoff.
An in-flight collision with a bird during cruise flight.

The failure of maintenance personnel to properly maintain the cargo door latch, resulting in an in-flight opening and separation of the cargo door, and substantial damage to the horizontal stabilator when it was struck by remnants of the cargo door.
The pilot's failure to maintain an appropriate descent rate during gusty winds while landing, resulting in a hard landing and damage to the airplane.
The improper installation of the connecting rod bolts, which resulted in an engine failure.
An in-flight encounter with unforecast turbulence, which resulted in structural damage to the stabilator.
A bearing failure that resulted in fatigue failure of the crankshaft and a subsequent total loss of engine power.
The pilot's failure to compensate for gusty wind conditions during the landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing and subsequent nose landing gear collapse.
The pilot’s unstabilized approach and improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
The pilot’s failure to properly configure the airplane for landing, which resulted in a gear-up landing.
The failure of the left main landing gear upper drag leg arm due to substandard mechanical properties, which resulted in a collapse of the landing gear upon landing.
The pilot's failure to attain an established approach path while on final approach resulting in an improper flare and bounced landing.
The pilot's delayed decision to abort a takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion.
The pilot’s loss of airplane control while landing with a gusting wind.

The pilot's improper touchdown point during landing, which resulted in a runway overrun. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s decision to land with a tailwind condition and his lack of recent experience.
The Boeing 747 first officer’s failure to maintain clearance from another airplane while taxiing due to his inadequate judgment of the distance between the airplanes.

The tug driver’s loss of airplane control during pushback due to a loss of traction in slippery conditions on the ramp. The emergency ground egress during which a passenger broke her ankle. Contributing to the accident was the failure of the environmental system, which allowed smoke from a nearby house fire to enter the airplane.
The malfunction of the airplane’s aileron control system due to ice accumulation.
Moisture ingression thru the window humpseal coming into contact with the terminal block braid wires.
the improper retraction of the main cabin door, which resulted in the flight attendant falling when she opened the door at the destination.

The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power wires while maneuvering at a low altitude.
An in-flight fire and subsequent loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined due to extensive fire damage to the airplane and its fuel and electrical systems.
The pilot's failure to see and avoid powerlines during low-altitude agricultural spraying flight operations.
An in-flight collision with a bird during takeoff, which resulted in a partial loss of engine power and subsequent collision with trees and terrain.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing in a gusting crosswind, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with a hangar.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.

The loss of engine power for undetermined reasons, because the airplane wreckage was sold and relocated before the engine could be examined.
An in-flight structural failure due to a severely corroded wing strut, which resulted in a loss of airplane control.
The pilot’s improper landing flare which resulted in a bounced landing and the nose landing gear collapsing.
A loss of engine power due to the fatigue failure of the engine’s flywheel screws that were likely overloaded when the engine was involved in a previous accident.

The flight instructor’s decision to continue to taxi the airplane to the parking area with a known brake malfunction, which resulted in a loss of directional control and subsequent impact with a parked airplane.
The pilot’s inadequate compensation for gusting wind during the landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
The pilot's failure to ensure that the brake was fully engaged and his subsequent failure to notice that his airplane was rolling forward, which resulted in it hitting another airplane.

The pilot’s complacency during the en route phase of flight, which resulted in fuel mismanagement and a subsequent gear-up landing.
